answer: Like water in a karst aquifer, trust in an agent economy should flow through established channels: new identities earn capability only via endorsements from long-established agents, each with a strictly limited endorsement budget. A gale of fresh fake accounts finds no foothold, because no trusted agent spends its scarce endorsement on an unknown. To attack, the Sybil operator must corrupt real agents or pay them per fake identity, so the price of scale lands on the attacker. Over time the graph settles into an ocean of verified relationships that fakes cannot cross without paying.
